title: Back Pain

rationale.Physical Exam: Neuro / Rectal tone: Saddle anesthesia, decreased rectal tone, bilateral weakness.
rationale.EMERGENCY MRI lumbar spine: Do not delay. Confirm cauda equina compression.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with severe low back pain, bilateral leg weakness and numbness, saddle anesthesia (perineal numbness), urinary retention/incontinence, fecal incontinence, and decreased rectal tone. These are the RED FLAG symptoms of cauda equina syndrome — compression of the cauda equina nerve roots below the conus medullaris. This is a SURGICAL EMERGENCY. Delay in decompression leads to permanent paralysis, incontinence, and sexual dysfunction. Most common cause: massive central disc herniation. Other causes: trauma, tumor, abscess, hematoma. Diagnosis: EMERGENCY MRI of lumbar spine (do NOT wait). Post-void residual (PVR) >200mL supports diagnosis. Treatment: EMERGENCY neurosurgical decompression (laminectomy + discectomy) within 24-48 hours of symptom onset.
